relevance_note: Case report of one adult with arterial tortuosity syndrome ('A 27-year-old patient with ATS'), with individual-level clinical detail; father and sibling also had arterial tortuosity on CT angiography.
method_note: Read the full paper manually; output assembled with a short Python script from hand-written values. Scope: the index patient (label 'patient'), father and sibling (arterial tortuosity on family CT screening; family ATS diagnosis 'reestablished with genetic testing'), and the previously published adult ATS patient of Aliramezany et al (ref 17; individual-level pulmonary artery pressure given). No variants rows: genetic testing is mentioned but no gene or variant is attributed to the patient or relatives (SLC2A10 is named only in the general Discussion), so no row was created. Other cited cases (refs 6, 7, 18, 23) are given no individual-level facts in the text (ref 7's 51-year-old woman and variant appear only in the reference-list title), so no rows. Contradiction: text gives baseline mean PAP 80 mm Hg and PVR 20.9 WU, while Table 1 (May 2018) gives mean PAP 84 mm Hg and PVR 20.39 WU. Age '27-year-old' recorded as age at last evaluation/report; the sentence ('A 27-year-old patient ... was referred to the clinic 8 years ago') could also be read as age at referral. Father and sibling: 'arterial tortuosity' without location, so aortic and non-aortic tortuosity checklist items left not reported. Dyspnea and lung edema not mapped to 'respiratory distress or insufficiency'; dilated right heart chambers not mapped to ventricular hypertrophy. Vital status left not reported (alive implied by ongoing follow-up but not stated). Ref 17 patient's PAP 120 mm Hg not mapped to the pulmonary hypertension checklist item because the paper does not call it pulmonary hypertension.
